prompt: What did streaming change in `timing.py`?
hint: Compare the two lines number by number.

choices.text: The total time, from 13.6 s to 0.3 s
choices.why: The totals were 13.6 and 14.8 s.

choices.text: It made the model write fewer tokens
choices.why: The two replies were two draws, 132 and 154 tokens.
Right: after 0.3 s instead of 13.6.
The tokens cost the same either way.

prompt: In seconds, how long did the whole streamed reply take?
hint: The last number on the stream line.

prompt: The first token takes four seconds and the rest follows quickly. Where should you look first?
hint: Which part of the work happens before the first token?

choices.why: That limits the output, which is fast here.
Right: the prompt's length and the cache; the model reads all of it before writing.

choices.text: At the renderer in the page
choices.why: The page has nothing to render yet.

choices.text: At the network between page and relay
choices.why: The relay has had nothing to pass on.

prompt: Which of these gains nothing from streaming?
hint: Who would see the first word?

choices.why: A person reads it as it arrives.
A person is waiting at the cursor.

choices.text: The reply box on a support page a customer is reading
choices.why: A person is watching it.

choices.text: A nightly job that files tickets as JSON
choices.why: Right: a program needs the whole reply, and nobody is watching.

prompt: Put the events of a streamed text reply in order.
How does a reader know a streamed reply is complete?

choices.why: Right: a close without it is a reply that did not finish.
A connection can close halfway.

choices.text: No piece arrived for a second
choices.why: A slow model pauses too.

choices.text: The text ends with a full stop
choices.why: Text says nothing about the stream.

prompt: Anthropic's API sends `ping` events in a stream and Ollama sends none. What are they for?

choices.why: They carry no time.

choices.text: Asking the client to confirm it is still there
choices.why: Server-sent events go one way.
Right: something in between might close it.

choices.text: Marking the end of the reply
choices.why: That is `message_stop`.

prompt: A stream of server-sent events has the content type ___.
Why does `C|ents` arrive as two pieces?

choices.text: The network split the word between two packets
choices.why: The pieces are the provider's, before the network.

choices.text: Pieces follow tokens, and the word is two
choices.why: Right: the tokenizer split it.
The SDK joins pieces; it does not split them.

choices.text: The relay buffered half of it
choices.why: There is no relay in `pieces.py`.

prompt: A page adds a space between pieces. What does the reader see?

choices.text: Nothing different from the reply itself
choices.why: Pieces are not words.
No piece was capitalised.
Pieces do not repeat.
Right: append each piece as it is.

prompt: Match each API's stream to how it says the reply ended.
Where did `end_turn 18 in, 144 out` come from?

choices.why: Right: the message the SDK built when the stream ended.
That knows the input, not the output.
There was one request.
The bars count pieces, and they print nothing at the end.

prompt: Why does the page talk to a relay instead of the model's API?
hint: What would the page need to hold?

choices.why: `fetch` reads them, as `client.mjs` shows.

choices.text: The relay makes the reply faster
choices.why: It adds a hop; it does not speed the model.

choices.text: The request needs the API key
choices.why: Right: anything in a page can be read by whoever uses it.
That is not the reason the section gives.

prompt: Why does `client.mjs` keep `buffer` between reads?
hint: Where can a network read end?

choices.text: To retry a read that failed with a network error
choices.why: Nothing is retried.
Right: one ends mid-event, and the half after the last blank line waits for the rest.
It displays as fast as events complete.
The relay sends none.

prompt: What must the relay also do, besides passing pieces on? Choose all that apply.
hint: It spends money on every question.

choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Limit the length and rate of questions
choices.why: Yes: one user could use up everyone's limit.

choices.text: Send the API key to the page once
choices.why: Never: that is what the relay exists to avoid.

choices.text: Make sure nothing on the way buffers the response
choices.why: Yes: buffering removes the stream without an error.

prompt: In the log after Stop, Ollama had `n_tokens = 47`, and 38 of them were the question. How many tokens of the reply had it written?
How does `cancel.py` stop the reply?
hint: What happens when the loop is left?

choices.text: It sends a stop request to the API
choices.why: There is no such request in the script.
That was fixed before the request.
It leaves before then.
Right: and leaving it closes the response.

prompt: A person closes the tab. What must the relay do?

choices.text: Finish reading the reply and store it
choices.why: Nobody will see it, and it is billed.

choices.text: Close its own request to the provider
choices.why: Right: otherwise it pays for a reply nobody reads.
Nobody asked again.
A stop is a person's choice, not a failure.

prompt: Why does a stream's failure arrive as an event and not as a status code?

choices.text: The status went out as 200 with the first byte
choices.why: Right: it cannot be changed afterwards.

choices.text: Status codes are not allowed in streams
choices.why: Every HTTP response has one.
It reports them, on plain requests.
Speed is not the reason.

prompt: How many characters had reached the screen when the stream broke?
A stream breaks after half a paragraph and the page retries on its own. What must it do with the new reply?
hint: The new reply starts from the first word.

choices.text: Append it to what is shown
choices.why: That repeats a sentence and a half.

choices.text: Show it only if it matches the first half
choices.why: Two replies to one question need not match.
Right: and the person can see it restarted.

choices.text: Discard it and keep the half
choices.why: Half a paragraph is not an answer.

prompt: When can the host run a streamed tool call?
hint: When does the JSON parse, on any server?

choices.why: No argument has arrived yet.
On Ollama that is the whole object; on Anthropic's API it can be half of one.

choices.text: As soon as the SKU looks complete
choices.why: `LAM` looks like no SKU, and `LAMP-0` looks like one.
Right: at `content_block_stop`, or from the final message.

prompt: A tool call's arguments arrive in events whose delta type is ___.
After 16 pieces the text ends in `**`. What does a tolerant Markdown renderer show?
hint: An opening marker with no close.

choices.why: That is the other strategy, waiting for complete blocks.
Right: two literal asterisks until the close arrives.
A tolerant renderer does not fail on it.
There is no text to make bold yet.

prompt: How should a screen reader hear a streamed reply?
hint: A live region reads every change.

choices.text: Once complete, or a sentence at a time
choices.why: Right: something a listener can follow.
That reads out fragments, one after another.

choices.text: Not at all, to avoid noise
choices.why: Then a blind reader never hears the answer.
The rest of the answer matters too.

prompt: Match each moment of a stream to what the page should do.

pairs.right: Show that the reply is coming
Mark the partial text as cut off
Close the stream to the provider

right_distractors: Retry and append the new reply

prompt: A team adds streaming to its support chat. Which plan follows this lesson?

choices.text: Call the provider from the page with a key limited to chat
choices.why: Any key in a page can be read and used.

choices.text: Stream from the relay and retry silently on any error, appending the new text
choices.why: Appending a retry repeats the start of the reply.

choices.text: Relay holds the key; Stop closes upstream; errors marked
choices.why: Right: each piece of this lesson.

choices.text: Stream everything, including the nightly ticket job
choices.why: A program needs the whole reply; nobody watches it.
